objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will have delivered a short podcast-style talk on their chosen topic, using functional phrases for opening, persuading, structuring, and closing arguments within a 60â€â€œ90 second time limit.
materials: - Follow-on from previous lesson: OFD 3, Unit 1, pp. 10-11 (Understanding Podcasts)

stages.stage_aim: To help learners settle back into their podcast project by recalling last session's planning work and clarifying the baseline recording goal
stages.procedure:
- As Ss enter, direct them to sit next to their podcast partner and pull out their planning sheet.
- Quick recall: 'What podcast topic did you plan? You have 30 seconds to remind your partner.' Then take 2 rapid-fire answers from pairs.
- Announce the goal: 'Today youâ€™re going to record your podcast — 60 to 90 seconds. One take only. No retakes. This is your baseline recording.'
- Frame the purpose: 'This is a snapshot of where you are right now. In a few months, youâ€™ll listen back and see how much youâ€™ve improved.'

stages.stage_aim: To present the three role formats clearly and equip learners with a toolkit of functional phrases for their podcast scripts
stages.procedure:
- Display the three role combinations (A, B, and C) as a table on the board or slide:
  • A (Co-hosts) — S1 opens + Argument 1; S2 delivers Argument 2 + closing. Equal split.
  • B (Host + Guest) — S1 (Host) opens, introduces the guest, asks 2 questions; S2 (Guest) answers with examples and advice.
  • C (Debate Duo) — S1 argues FOR; S2 argues AGAINST and closes.
- Walk through each in 20 seconds per option. Emphasise: both partners speak 30â€â€œ45 seconds regardless.
- Directive: '30 seconds to decide. If you canâ€™t decide, I assign A. Go.' Count down. Thumbs-up check.
- Transition to phrases: 'Here are phrases to make your podcast sound natural.' Display:
  • Openings (all): 'Welcome to my podcastâ€¦', 'Today Iâ€™m going to talk aboutâ€¦', 'Iâ€™m joined today byâ€¦'
  • Persuading (A, B): 'Have you ever thought aboutâ€¦?', 'You might not realise this, butâ€¦', 'Hereâ€™s something to considerâ€¦'
  • Structuring (all): 'First of allâ€¦', 'Another point isâ€¦', 'On the other handâ€¦', 'So, to sum upâ€¦'
- Choral drilling: all-class repeat (1 round), then rows (1 round). Focus on conversational rhythm, not robot reading.
- 'Annotate your planning sheet — circle the phrases for your combination.'

stages.stage_aim: To give learners a low-stakes opportunity to try out the target phrases in short timed turns before writing their scripts
stages.procedure:
- 'Exercise A — Mini-monologue drill. Stay with your assigned partner.'
- Round 1 (2 min): Student 1 delivers a 30-second mini-monologue on any topic using at least 2 target phrases. Student 2 counts the phrases silently.
- Round 2 (2 min): Switch. Student 2 delivers a 30-second mini-monologue on a different topic. Student 1 counts.
- Quick feedback (1 min): Teacher highlights 1 strong example and corrects 1 common error — e.g., flat intonation. Model the difference between reading aloud and conversational podcast delivery.

stages.stage_aim: To guide learners in writing a timed script that fits both their chosen role combination and the 60â€â€œ90 second limit
stages.procedure:
- Start an 8-minute countdown timer on the board — keep it visible.
- 'Use your planning sheet. Write a script that matches your combination.'
- Role-specific instructions:
  • A: S1 writes opening + Argument 1. S2 writes Argument 2 + closing.
  • B: S1 (Host) writes opening, guest intro, 2 questions. S2 (Guest) writes answers with examples and advice.
  • C: S1 writes argument FOR. S2 writes argument AGAINST + closing.
- Display checklist:
  ? Clear opening
  ? At least 2 arguments or advice points
  ? At least 3 target phrases from Stage 2
  ? A short closing
  ? 60â€â€œ90 seconds when spoken aloud
- Circulate fast. Check each pair's role distribution. Call time at 4 min and 1 min. Push for natural spoken language — discourage written-sounding sentences.

stages.stage_aim: To let learners practise their delivery aloud and fine-tune the timing and naturalness of their script before recording
stages.procedure:
- 'Three minutes to rehearse. Time yourselves.'
- Round 1 (2 min): Ss practise with scripts. Partner gives feedback: 'Too fast? Too slow? Can you hear the target phrases?' Partner raises hand at 60 seconds to check timing.
- Round 2 (1 min): Ss practise again aiming for limited script use — look up, sound conversational.
- Teacher moves between pairs giving rapid-fire coaching: 'Louder opening.' 'Youâ€™re at 50 seconds — need more.' 'That phrase sounded natural — keep it.'

stages.stage_aim: To capture a clean baseline recording of each pairâ€™s podcast as a starting point for tracking speaking progress across the academic year
stages.procedure:
- Set up a recording device (phone or laptop) at the front. 'One take only. No restarts. This is your baseline.'
- 'When I call your pair name, come to the front, deliver your podcast, sit down. Everyone else — absolutely silent.'
- Call pairs in sequence. Each pair delivers their 60â€â€œ90 second podcast. Teacher records without offering feedback, corrections, or gestures during the recording.
- Between recordings, call the next pair immediately — no dead air, no commentary on the previous performance.
- With the longer recording window, stagger efficiently: call up the next pair while the previous pair is sitting down. Aim for ~90 seconds per pair (60â€â€œ90s podcast + 10â€â€œ20s transition). For a class of 10â€â€œ12 pairs, this fits comfortably in the 20-minute block with time to spare.
- If all pairs finish early, use any remaining time for a second take for pairs who feel their first was unrepresentative (still baseline — no coaching). If not all pairs get through, the remaining pairs record at the start of the next lesson.

stages.stage_aim: To encourage learners to reflect on the recording experience and to reinforce the value of this baseline as a reference point for future progress
stages.procedure:
- Display two reflection prompts on the board: 'What was the hardest part? What went better than you expected?'
- 'Discuss with your partner for 60 seconds. No whole-class feedback — this is a private reflection for yourselves.'
- After 60 seconds, deliver the closing statement: 'That recording is your starting point. In a few months, youâ€™ll listen back and see how far youâ€™ve come. Well done today — good pace, good focus.'
- Dismiss.
